title: PATENT RESEARCH REPORT
abstract: This technical report synthesizes patent research data on the polymerization and synthesis of Low Acrylonitrile Nitrile Butadiene Rubber (Low ACN NBR), focusing on a selected patent landscape comprising US9650502, US9034992, US7923518, US8389623, US8436091, and US8664340. Low ACN NBR, typically defined by a bound acrylonitrile content ranging from 27% to 36%, is highly valued for its low-temperature flexibility, oil resistance, and elastomeric performance. The patent landscape reveals that emulsion polymerization is the dominant synthesis pathway, predominantly conducted under cold conditions (7 to 8 degrees Celsius) to optimize polymer structure and minimize branching. Key process trends include the utilization of advanced redox initiator systems, such as diisopropylbenzene hydroperoxide (DIHP) or p-menthane hydroperoxide coupled with reducing agents like sodium formaldehyde sulfoxylate (FSS) or Rongalit C, and iron-based catalysts. Precise molecular weight control is achieved through the incremental addition of chain-transfer agents like tertiary dodecyl mercaptan (TDM/t-DDM) during polymerization. Furthermore, post-polymerization coagulation and washing processes are heavily emphasized across the patents. The choice of coagulant (magnesium sulfate, magnesium chloride, calcium chloride, or sodium chloride) and the control of latex pH prior to coagulation are critical factors in determining the residual ion indices of the final rubber. These ionic concentrations directly influence vulcanization kinetics, Mooney scorch safety, and corrosion resistance in sealing applications. This report provides a comprehensive cross-patent comparison and methodology extraction to guide future formulation and process optimization.

patent_details.patent_title: Process for the preparation of nitrile rubbers
patent_details.assignee: Not disclosed in the analyzed patent evidence
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Discloses a cold emulsion polymerization process for low ACN nitrile rubbers with bound ACN contents of 27.9% to 28.1%.

polymerization_method.monomer_ratio: 500 g acrylonitrile to 4.37 kg butadiene (Latex A/C) or 815 g acrylonitrile to 4.0 kg butadiene (Latex B)
polymerization_method.emulsifier: Potassium stearate and DNMK (disproportionated rosin acid salt derivative)
polymerization_method.emulsifier_loading: 0.53 kg of 5.4 wt% potassium stearate solution and 0.440 kg DNMK
polymerization_method.chain_transfer_dosage: 18.72 g initial, with booster additions of 2.34 g at 37% and 59% conversion
polymerization_method.coagulation_conditions: Latex added to 43 kg water and 4 kg saturated magnesium sulfate solution at elevated temperature
polymerization_method.post_treatment: Washing with deionized water at pH 11.5-11.8 (adjusted with KOH), filtering, and drying at 100 degrees Celsius for 24 hours
polymerization_method.raw_polymer_properties: Bound ACN: 27.9% - 28.1% (Latex A/C) and 33.9% (Latex B); Mooney Viscosity: 29.0 - 60.5 MU

experimental_evidence: Latex A was prepared using 500 g acrylonitrile and 4.37 kg butadiene, yielding a bound ACN content of 28.1% and a Mooney viscosity of 60.5 MU.
Latex C was prepared under similar conditions to Latex A, yielding a bound ACN content of 27.9% and a Mooney viscosity of 29.0 MU.
Latex B utilized 815 g acrylonitrile and 4.0 kg butadiene, resulting in a higher bound ACN content of 33.9% and a Mooney viscosity of 32.1 MU.
Coagulation was performed using magnesium sulfate, and the resulting crumbs were washed at pH 11.5-11.8 to control residual emulsifier levels.
methodology_patents.technical_relevance: This patent provides a detailed recipe for synthesizing NBR with low bound ACN (27.9% - 28.1%) using a cold emulsion process and a staged chain-transfer agent addition strategy.

experimental_evidence: NBR latex was coagulated using a magnesium chloride solution containing an acid-ashed gelatin with a viscosity of 92.1 cP and an isoelectric point of 8.7.
Vulcanized test specimens were produced by pressing at 160 degrees Celsius under 120 bar for 30 minutes.
Sealing rings made from the vulcanizates showed excellent corrosion resistance when stored between aluminum plates at 80% relative humidity and 70 degrees Celsius.
methodology_patents.technical_relevance: This patent highlights the importance of coagulation additives, specifically acid-ashed gelatin in combination with magnesium chloride, to minimize the corrosive tendency of low ACN NBR in sealing applications.

experimental_evidence: NBR latices coagulated with magnesium chloride displayed lower Mooney scorch, shorter vulcanization times, and higher stresses at 300% elongation compared to non-inventive coagulation methods.
Vulcanizate properties were shown to depend heavily on the concentration and relative ratio of cations remaining in the nitrile rubber.
methodology_patents.technical_relevance: This patent demonstrates that the choice of salt during coagulation (specifically magnesium chloride vs calcium chloride) directly influences the vulcanization kinetics and mechanical properties of the rubber.

patent_details.assignee: Not disclosed in the analyzed patent evidence
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Discloses a highly detailed emulsion polymerization recipe for NBR with an ACN content of approximately 35-36% using a specific iron-based redox system.

polymerization_method.monomer_ratio: 61.4 parts butadiene, 36 parts acrylonitrile, 2.6 parts 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate
polymerization_method.catalyst_activator: Premix FeSO4 or FeCl2 (0.030 parts by weight) with Rongalit C (2.0 g in premix) and EDTA
polymerization_method.coagulation_conditions: Admixed with a 50% dispersion of Vulkanox BKF (0.3% by weight based on NBR solids) prior to coagulation
polymerization_method.post_treatment: Washing with 1 to 5 parts by weight of water per 100 parts of NBR
polymerization_method.raw_polymer_properties: ACN content: 35.3% - 36.6%; Mooney viscosity: 25 - 142 MU; Glass transition temperature (Tg): -25.8 to -23.1 degrees Celsius

experimental_evidence: Nitrile rubber G (using FeSO4 premix) reached 86.1% conversion in 7.0 hours, yielding a polymer with a Tg of -23.9 degrees Celsius.
Nitrile rubber H (using FeCl2 premix) reached 84.2% conversion in 6.5 hours, yielding a polymer with a Tg of -23.7 degrees Celsius.
The use of FeCl2 instead of FeSO4 in the redox system resulted in distinct polymer properties, including differences in the Mooney viscosity and ACN distribution.
methodology_patents.technical_relevance: This patent provides a precise, comparative recipe demonstrating how minor changes in the redox catalyst system (FeSO4 vs FeCl2) affect the polymerization rate, conversion, and final low-temperature properties of NBR.

polymerization_method.raw_polymer_properties: Controlled ion indices; vulcanizates show higher vulcanization rates (t90-t10) and higher stress at 30% elongation (4.2 - 10.2 MPa)

experimental_evidence: Latex pH was adjusted to 9.5 using KOH for comparative run C6, and to 5.8 using HCl for run C13, prior to coagulation.
Coagulation with CaCl2 (0.3 to 1.2 wt%) at 20 degrees Celsius yielded rubbers with high vulcanization rates and stress values at 30% elongation (up to 10.2 MPa).
Washing with deionized water (DW) was shown to be more effective at controlling final ion indices than washing with brackish water (BW).
methodology_patents.technical_relevance: This patent establishes the critical role of pre-coagulation pH adjustment and wash-water quality in determining the final ionic profile and vulcanization performance of NBR.
